ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
During the ripening process of banana fruit, the stored substances in the fruit are continuously metabolically transformed, and the banana gradually becomes sweet. In Figure A, curves I and II respectively indicate the changing trends of the contents of two substances during the ripening process of banana fruit. Please answer:
Take equal amounts of banana pulp ripened to day X and day Y, respectively add equal amounts of distilled water to make extracts. Then add 5 mL of the extract from day X to each of test tubes a and b, and add 5 mL of the extract from day Y to each of test tubes c and d, as shown in Figure B. Add equal amounts of Fehling's reagent to each of test tubes b and d, and after boiling, tube b shows a brick-red color. Compared with tube b, is the color of tube d deeper or lighter?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: During the ripening process of banana fruit, the stored substances in the fruit are continuously metabolically transformed, and the banana gradually becomes sweet. In Figure A, curves I and II respectively indicate the changing trends of the contents of two substances during the ripening process of banana fruit. Please answer: Take equal amounts of banana pulp ripened to day X and day Y, respectively add equal amounts of distilled water to make extracts. Then add 5 mL of the extract from day X to each of test tubes a and b, and add 5 mL of the extract from day Y to each of test tubes c and d, as shown in Figure B. Add equal amounts of Fehling's reagent to each of test tubes b and d, and after boiling, tube b shows a brick-red color. Compared with tube b, is the color of tube d deeper or lighter?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the horizontal axis of Figure A is labeled ripening time (d), and the vertical axis is labeled the contents of two substances; X is located at an earlier ripening time, and Y is located at a later ripening time. Curve I gradually decreases as ripening time is prolonged, and curve II gradually increases as ripening time is prolonged, so by day Y, the content of the substance corresponding to curve II is higher than on day X. In Figure B, test tubes a and b are added with the extract from day X, and test tubes c and d are added with the extract from day Y; among them, test tubes b and d are also added with equal amounts of Fehling's reagent and boiled. Then reason: the stem states that during the ripening process bananas gradually become sweet, indicating that the reducing sugar content increases in the later stage of ripening, so the rising curve II in Figure A represents the change in reducing sugar content. Fehling's reagent is used to detect reducing sugars; the more reducing sugar there is, the more brick-red precipitate is produced after boiling, and the deeper the color. The reducing sugar content in the extract from day Y is higher than that from day X, therefore tube d has a deeper color than tube b.
